items.title: What to Expect From Agilent Technologies' Q3 2026 Earnings Report
items.summary: Agilent Technologies is poised to release its third-quarter results soon, and analysts are projecting a single-digit earnings rise.

items.title: Can GE HealthCare Sustain Growth in Q2 Amid Persistent Cost Headwinds?
items.summary: GE HealthCare heads into Q2 earnings season with solid revenue drivers, but inflation and tariff costs may keep margins under pressure before an expected second-half recovery.

items.title: Will Baxter's Q2 Results Continue to Reflect Operational Headwinds?
items.summary: BAX's second-quarter results may reflect pressured earnings and sales as manufacturing inefficiencies, inflation, and product holds offset steady demand across segments.

items.title: 1 Healthcare Stock to Research Further and 2 We Avoid
items.summary: From novel pharmaceuticals to telemedicine, most healthcare companies are on a mission to drive better patient outcomes. Shareholders who bet on the industry have been rewarded lately as healthcare stocks have returned 9.7% over the past six months, topping the S&P 500 by 1.8 percentage points.

items.title: Reading Between The Lines Of DHR's Latest Call
items.summary: Danaher's latest earnings call saw analysts repeatedly test one sore spot in an otherwise solid quarter, and management's answers reveal the key risk for investors now.

items.title: 1 of Wall Street’s Favorite Stocks on Our Buy List and 2 We Brush Off
items.summary: The stocks in this article have caught Wall Street’s attention in a big way, with price targets implying returns above 20%. But investors should take these forecasts with a grain of salt because analysts typically say nice things about companies so their firms can win business in other product lines like M&A advisory.

items.title: Alamar Hits A High Note On Alzheimer's Buzz
items.summary: If you’re an Alamar Biosciences (ALMR) shareholder, Friday was a good day. The stock climbed +7.3%, closing the session at a new 52-week high of $28.42. That’s a tidy gain on a day when the S&P 500 barely nudged up +0.4% and some key industry peers actually lost ground.

items.title: Agilent (A): Buy, Sell, or Hold Post Q1 Earnings?
items.summary: Over the past six months, Agilent’s stock price fell to $134.31. Shareholders have lost 8.2% of their capital, which is disappointing considering the S&P 500 has climbed by 8.4%. This may have investors wondering how to approach the situation.
